messages.subject: Discordant classification for two similar reads using featureCounts --read2pos
messages.subject_clean: Discordant classification for two similar reads using featureCounts --read2pos
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am having trouble understanding how two very similar reads give different results when using featureCounts with --read2pos.

Here are the two reads:

$ zcat 2016-03-31.fastq.gz
@HWI-700819F:303:C6WYKACXX:2:2113:9364:95721:UMI_AAAAGGGG 1:N:0:AGGGAAGC
GCTGTTCTACAGCTATGGCCGGGCCAGCTGCAGCTTTCCGCCGCTTGGGCGCCTTGTCCGGAGCTGCGGCCTTAGGCTTCGCTTCCTACGGG
+
FFFFFIIIIIFIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIFFFFFFFFFFFBFFFBFBBBBBFFFBFFFFFBFFFFFBFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFB
@HWI-700819F:303:C6WYKACXX:2:2314:4761:64177:UMI_AAAAGGGG 1:N:0:AGGGAAGC
GCTGTTCTACAGCTATGGCCGGGCCAGCTGCAGCTTTCCGCCGCTTGGGCGCCTTGTCCGGAGCTGCGGCCTTAGGCTTCGCTTC
+
FFBF<7BFFFFFIIFBFFFFFFF<BF<B0<BB<BBBFBBFFBBBBBB<<07BBB<<<<BBB7<<BB<7<B<00<<BB<<B7<7BB

They start the same, but are different lengths because they were quality trimmed from the 3' end. When I search with BLAT, they are similar as expected. They both map to the reverse strand, have the same end position (their 5' end), and the match starts at the second base of the query sequence (the first G does not map to the genome).

   ACTIONS      QUERY           SCORE START  END QSIZE IDENTITY CHRO STRAND  START    END      SPAN
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
browser <http://www.genome.ucsc.edu/cgi-bin/hgTracks?position=chr17:7307326-7307416&db=hg19&ss=../trash/hgSs/hgSs_www_4293_ddab90.pslx+../trash/hgSs/hgSs_www_4293_ddab90.fa&hgsid=485870845_CKaQawArt2WNyAkEyBsAQugE1HFq> details <http://www.genome.ucsc.edu/cgi-bin/hgc?o=7307325&g=htcUserAli&i=../trash/hgSs/hgSs_www_4293_ddab90.pslx+..%2Ftrash%2FhgSs%2FhgSs_www_4293_ddab90.fa+YourSeq&c=chr17&l=7307325&r=7307416&db=hg19&hgsid=485870845_CKaQawArt2WNyAkEyBsAQugE1HFq> YourSeq           91     2    92    92 100.0%    17   -    7307326   7307416     91

  ACTIONS      QUERY           SCORE START  END QSIZE IDENTITY CHRO STRAND  START    END      SPAN
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
browser <http://www.genome.ucsc.edu/cgi-bin/hgTracks?position=chr17:7307333-7307416&db=hg19&ss=../trash/hgSs/hgSs_www_454f_ddb450.pslx+../trash/hgSs/hgSs_www_454f_ddb450.fa&hgsid=485870845_CKaQawArt2WNyAkEyBsAQugE1HFq> details <http://www.genome.ucsc.edu/cgi-bin/hgc?o=7307332&g=htcUserAli&i=../trash/hgSs/hgSs_www_454f_ddb450.pslx+..%2Ftrash%2FhgSs%2FhgSs_www_454f_ddb450.fa+YourSeq&c=chr17&l=7307332&r=7307416&db=hg19&hgsid=485870845_CKaQawArt2WNyAkEyBsAQugE1HFq> YourSeq           84     2    85    85 100.0%    17   -    7307333   7307416     84

I map these to sequences to human genome hg19 with subjunc:

$ subjunc -i genome/combined -r 2016-03-31.fastq.gz -u > 2016-03-31.bam

Already at this step the two sequences start to diverge. Both have one non-matching base, but only the first read has the soft-clipped base in its CIGAR.

$ samtools view 2016-03-31.bam
HWI-700819F:303:C6WYKACXX:2:2113:9364:95721:UMI_AAAAGGGG    16    chr17    7307326    59    91M1S    *    0    0    CCCGTAGGAAGCGAAGCCTAAGGCCGCAGCTCCGGACAAGGCGCCCAAGCGGCGGAAAGCTGCAGCTGGCCCGGCCATAGCTGTAGAACAGC    BFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFBFFFFFBFFFFFBFFFBBBBBFBFFFBFFFFFFFFFFFIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIFIIIIIFFFFF    HI:i:1    NH:i:1    NM:i:0
HWI-700819F:303:C6WYKACXX:2:2314:4761:64177:UMI_AAAAGGGG    16    chr17    7307333    58    85M    *    0    0    GAAGCGAAGCCTAAGGCCGCAGCTCCGGACAAGGCGCCCAAGCGGCGGAAAGCTGCAGCTGGCCCGGCCATAGCTGTAGAACAGC    BB7<7B<<BB<<00<B<7<BB<<7BBB<<<<BBB70<<BBBBBBFFBBFBBB<BB<0B<FB<FFFFFFFBFIIFFFFFB7<FBFF    HI:i:1    NH:i:1    NM:i:1

Next I use featureCounts to get gene counts.

$ featureCounts -a 2016-03-31.saf -F SAF -R -s 1 --read2pos 5 -o 2016-03-31.txt 2016-03-31.bam

I use strand-specific counting and reduce the read to the most 5' base. Because of the BLAT results that the 5 ' ends of both sequences map to chr17:7,307,416, I'd expect featureCounts to give the same assignment for both sequences. However, this is not the case. The first is determined to be ambiguous due to multi-mapping to 3 separate genes, but the second is assigned to just one of the three.

$ cat 2016-03-31.bam.featureCounts
HWI-700819F:303:C6WYKACXX:2:2113:9364:95721:UMI_AAAAGGGG    Unassigned_Ambiguity    *    Number_Of_Overlapped_Genes=3
HWI-700819F:303:C6WYKACXX:2:2314:4761:64177:UMI_AAAAGGGG    Assigned    ENSG00000205544    *

How is this possible? Is the soft-clipped base in the CIGAR of the one read changing the position featureCounts uses for read2pos? Is the correct end of the read being used? Since it is mapped to the reverse strand, the end position should be used. If I change `--read2pos` to 3 or do not use it, both reads are classified as ambiguous.

I am using the binary subread-1.5.0-p1-Linux-x86_64. All these files are available to download from Dropbox:

https://www.dropbox.com/s/ne6jwd0gsyfxgzj/2016-03-31.fastq.gz?dl=0
https://www.dropbox.com/s/dzawbx878dv0pyc/2016-03-31.bam?dl=0
https://www.dropbox.com/s/dkhzfq2ogvrnkeq/2016-03-31.txt?dl=0
https://www.dropbox.com/s/0b3fojp6hrc6xec/2016-03-31.txt.summary?dl=0
https://www.dropbox.com/s/43uiqpmmeazbont/2016-03-31.bam.featureCounts?dl=0

The SAF file only has the exons for the 3 genes needed to reproduce this issue:

https://www.dropbox.com/s/xri6yfmlsrrf8ez/2016-03-31.saf?dl=0

Thank you,

John

messages.subject_clean: Discordant classification for two similar reads using featureCounts --read2pos
messages.body_plain:
Hi John,

The inconsistency in the mapping of the two reads was caused by a bug in subjunc. We will fix it and release a patch soon.

featureCounts does the counting correctly. It ignores the soft-clipped bases and the two reads were reduced to different positions (1bp apart) which resulted in different assignment result.

Thanks for reporting the bug.

Best wishes,

Wei

messages.subject: El Capitan problems: "Abort Trap: 6"
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I've recently upgraded to MacOS 10.11, and it seems to have broken subread-align. Both making subread from source and using the precompiled binaries results in an "Abort Trap: 6" error when running the following command:

subread-align -I 200 --sv -P 6  -i <index> -r <WGS fastq file> -o <output file/directory> -t 1

It gives me the warning that I should run "ulimit -n 500", but even after doing that I get the same errors, always partway through the "finishing" step:

//====================== Running (04-Apr-2016 15:45:57) ======================\\
||                                                                            ||
|| The input file contains base space reads.                                  ||
|| The range of Phred scores observed in the data is [2,41]                   ||
|| Load the 1-th index block...                                               ||
|| Map reads...                                                               ||
||    0% completed, 0.0 mins elapsed, rate=5.9k reads per second              ||
||    5% completed, 3.2 mins elapsed, rate=5.9k reads per second              ||
||   10% completed, 6.4 mins elapsed, rate=5.9k reads per second              ||
||   15% completed, 9.6 mins elapsed, rate=5.9k reads per second              ||
|| Finish the 6,990,506 reads...                                              ||
||   16% completed,  10 mins elapsed, rate=5.8k reads per second              ||
||   17% completed,  10 mins elapsed, rate=5.9k reads per second              ||
||   18% completed,  11 mins elapsed, rate=6.0k reads per second              ||
||   18% completed,  11 mins elapsed, rate=6.0k reads per second              ||
Abort trap: 6

Googling just tells me that "Abort trap 6" is a problem in the C compiler (I guess?), which is why I tried to see if I could solve it by making it from source, but that didn't fix it.

Thanks in advance for any help here guys!

-dylan

messages.subject: Re: featureCounts on sorted bam (Rsubread)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kristen,

featureCounts will pair up the second and third reads and count them as one read pair. It will count the first read separately.

featureCounts uses read name, mapping location of the current read, mapping location of the mate read and HI tag to pair up reads. The first read can not be paired up with any other reads.

Cheers,
Wei

messages.body_plain:
Hi Wei,

Thanks for fixing this bug. Using my previous test files, I confirmed that subread-1.5.0-p2 <https://sourceforge.net/projects/subread/files/subread-1.5.0-p2/> gives the correct result.

$ subjunc -i genome/combined -r 2016-03-31.fastq.gz -u > 2016-03-31.bam

The second read now also has the soft-clipped base (84M1S instead of 85M).

$ samtools view 2016-03-31.bam
HWI-700819F:303:C6WYKACXX:2:2113:9364:95721:UMI_AAAAGGGG    16    chr17    7307326    59    91M1S    *    0    0    CCCGTAGGAAGCGAAGCCTAAGGCCGCAGCTCCGGACAAGGCGCCCAAGCGGCGGAAAGCTGCAGCTGGCCCGGCCATAGCTGTAGAACAGC    BFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFBFFFFFBFFFFFBFFFBBBBBFBFFFBFFFFFFFFFFFIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIFIIIIIFFFFF    HI:i:1    NH:i:1    NM:i:0

HWI-700819F:303:C6WYKACXX:2:2314:4761:64177:UMI_AAAAGGGG    16    chr17    7307333    59    84M1S    *    0    0    GAAGCGAAGCCTAAGGCCGCAGCTCCGGACAAGGCGCCCAAGCGGCGGAAAGCTGCAGCTGGCCCGGCCATAGCTGTAGAACAGC    BB7<7B<<BB<<00<B<7<BB<<7BBB<<<<BBB70<<BBBBBBFFBBFBBB<BB<0B<FB<FFFFFFFBFIIFFFFFB7<FBFF    HI:i:1    NH:i:1    NM:i:0

With the improved mapping, now the reads are both classified as ambiguous since they have the same 5' start position.

$ featureCounts -a 2016-03-31.saf -F SAF -R -s 1 --read2pos 5 -o 2016-03-31.txt 2016-03-31.bam

$ cat 2016-03-31.bam.featureCounts
HWI-700819F:303:C6WYKACXX:2:2113:9364:95721:UMI_AAAAGGGG    Unassigned_Ambiguity    *    Number_Of_Overlapped_Genes=3

HWI-700819F:303:C6WYKACXX:2:2314:4761:64177:UMI_AAAAGGGG    Unassigned_Ambiguity    *    Number_Of_Overlapped_Genes=3

John

The results are not identical if I run featureCounts on the same bam file twice, e.g.:

> subread-1.5.0-p2-Linux-x86_64/bin/featureCounts -a refFlat.mm9.140822.gtf -o Aligned.zip.stream.counts.txt -F GTF -g transcript_id -O -p Aligned.zip.stream.sorted.bam

Here is a log10-log10 scatter plot of the count output from the 2 commands:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-0hex9vtmxKg/VyKB5FryN9I/AAAAAAAAALQ/rwOgy5__Qr88UvPs3kVg69ABeDtQO1bTQCLcB/s1600/reproducibility.png>
